# Chapter Eighteen: War (The Clash of Steel)

WAR

They crested the hill at dusk and Corliss could make out the carts, horses and pillars of smoke rising from the forest near the city and cursed. She urged her horse a little faster, motioning to Maelen and Dara to follow. She descended the hill urging the best faster and nearly jumped out of her skin when a large white cat emerged from the treeline with a Silvan rider atop him. The horse did not take it as well and reared as the two approached.

“Warden, General Durass asks you attend him at the forward camp, it is safe to proceed the battle was won” The Silvan soldier stated and there was a pride in his voice an eye. “The fallen has saved us Warden, he has saved us all” and with that cryptic statement the ride turned and moved back into the woods. Corliss watched the cat as its muscles rippled under the skin, standing almost as tall as the horse she rode the reacture was beautiful in its lethality, she had never seen its like.

Dara and Maelen both stared in stark shock and silence as the creature disappeared. “That was” Dara began and couldn’t finish the words. From what he said I think your friend might have done won the damn war” she said shaking her head and motioning for the two of them to follow.

The trio nagigated through the ruins of the battlefield, Corliss could see legions of troops out on the field guarded by the Wardens. How had so many surrendered she wondered shaking her head. The damage near the base of the city looked as if two giants had tussled, trees and tree tunks thrown around carriages and carts strewn about, crushed and torn apart. “What happened?” Corliss asked to no one in particular as she continued to survey the damage. “The magic that was used…” Dara whispered, and Corliss turned to see the wide eyes of the woman as she looked over the field seeing something that obviously Corliss could not. “What does she mean?” the Warden asked looking to Maelen.

The Old man, still weak from his time in the dungeon nodded to the field. “Every mage has a special something, some way their powers manifest. Dara can see the aura of power; she can see what was done and the leftovers of magics used in an area” he said looking towards her. “So, where you simply see damage, she see’s the power that caused it and apparently it was a lot” he finished and motioned ahead. Corliss turned to see General Durass stepping out from beneath the overhang of the elevator courtyard and nodding to the three of them. Corliss nodded to the man, stopping the horse just short of the stonework that marked out the elevator area and stepping off of the horse. Looking over she could spot at least eight more of the large cats with riders on them, mud covered their flanks as they roved over the battlefield. The contrast against the snow-white fur made the dirty brown splotches stand out even more. “So, General I see you had a few surprises” she said still eyeing the cats and riders. Durass smiled showing off the full white teeth and laugh lines that framed the sparkling eyes, still high with victory. “We are a private people Warden, there is a lot you do not know about us” he simply said and motioned for her to join them. “Where is Uri?” she asked and Durass pointed up. “He is leading the heavy gun emplacements, fortunately we did not need them during the battle, but he still ensures they stand ready should the Empress try to attack again, the seers fell but those creatures retreated, we know not where they are” he said wincing.

“What happened here General?” Corliss asked turning back to survey the field. Durass shook his head as if still not able to believe it, but with the conviction of one who had seen something that was impossible “The Fallen, he happened, he took the field Warden and like an avenging angel he brough the enemy to there knees, he dispatched ten of the twelve champions of the Empress and her army surrendered to him, I have never seen anything like it” he finished still shaking his head, not able to believe what he himself saw. Corliss’s eyes widened “what are you talking about?” she said.

Durass simply shrugged “its as I said Warden, it was like nothing I had ever seen, but the fallen, the procephy, it must be all true” he whispered like a man who had seen a miracle and was still trying to process it. Corliss took one more look at the field and tried to imagine what the man had seen, was it possible one man had done this, one man had caused the surrender of an entire army. Shaking her head at the thought she turned to the General. “Where is the Mage General” she asked motioning to Maelan and Dara as they traversed up the hill, they too looking over the field. The General turned focusing on the two mages and smiled “You have found his friend” he said and motioned for the elevator “he is at my residence, please” Durass said motioning for the three of them to enter the cab.

The ride up to the city was quiet, just the gentle bumping of the cab making its way up the large tree as the three stood there reflecting on the carnage they had seen. The elevator opened and the three exited into a large crowd of people, everyone one of them facing the direction they needed to go. “Lorin” Boomed a voice from her left and she turned to see the smiling face of Uri, the bear of a man wading through the thick crowd of people until he reached her.

“This way” he said motioning for them to follow, they crossed the sea of onlookers and came to a place near the large rotary cannons that were placed along the rails, guards keeping the people clear of the weapons allowing the soldiers to work. “Where are you going?” he asked looking at the two mages and Corliss motioned towards the far street “Durass’s house, I am bringing this one to see Marcus” at the mention of the Mage’s name she could see a glimmer of fear pass across Uri’s face “What is it Ur?” she asked. For as long as she could remember Corliss had never seen Uri scared, the man feared nothing and yet for a moment she had seen something Corliss never thought she would see on her mentor’s face. “That man is, he is something else Corliss, I have never seen anything like it, what he did down there” he started searching for words “I am glad he is on our side” he finished and barked for two guards who rushed over, snapping to attention in front of the group. “Take them to the General’s house” he said and nodded to Corliss. “Go see the mage, just because everyone is celebrating doesn’t mean there isn’t still danger, those…things still escaped trying to keep these warriors on point is easy, the cilivians though, they want to party and are causing havoc and distraction throughout the entire city” he said eyeing the crowd annoyed.

Corliss looked at them still standing there, whispering to each other as they faced away from the small group of Wardens. “What are they doing Uri?” she asked, and the large man winced “They are here to see him, the fallen your Marcus” he said motioning to the Mages. “They think he is there savior, the legend come to life, I don’t know about you two, but I would remove your Mage before things get out of hand” Uri said to the two Mages who nodded.

The soldiers moved through the crowd, making a path for the trio as they came to stand before the General’s house, two guards stood out front and upon seeing Corliss they moved allowing entry to the three of them.

They entered the house standing in the foyer the place seemed like a ghost town, the gaggle of stewards who usually rushed around when people were here, weren’t present. Finally, the old woman who managed the place for the General emerged coming to stand in front of the group. “Master Mage is upstairs in the guest room” she said and then just as quickly disappeared through a door. Corliss shrugged at the other two and motioned fro them to follow. They ascended the stairs coming to the door of the guest room at the top of the stairs. The door was open and the three stood there in awe as Marcus stood facing away from them, his shirt off and his head lowered. But that wasn’t what caught their attention, over his entire back pulsed the bright blue runic script as if it too were alive, the pulses almost like a heartbeat as Marcus continued to stand their head lowered as if in contemplation.

Dara brushed past the two, coming into the room and crossing over to the Mage, turning he reguardded her, looking into his eye’s tears sprang from her and Dara threw her arms around him, sobbing openly. Corliss stood there suddenly uncomfortable, finally the two untangled themselves and Marcus turned, Corliss seeing the runes also covered his entire front as well. She had never seen anything like it and it scared the hell out of her. “Marcus, Maelen is saved” she simply said stepping out of the way as the smiling old man crossed the room and threw his arms around his student and friend.

“Its good to see your old man” Marcus said, his voice husky with emotion as the two continued to embrace, taking comfort from each other. Corliss gave them there moment but judging by the crowd outside she felt an itch in the center of her shoulder blades that just wouldn’t go away. She heard the front door open and turned to see Durass enter the house and rush up the stairs. He came to stand next to Corliss and looked into the room, his eyes locking on the glowing runes “by Aurtus” he whispered his eyes going even wider, if that were possible Corliss thought. “General?” Corliss said nudging the man out of his trance. With a start he turned to look at her “Marcus needs to get out of the city Warden, the council, im sorry but they consider him a threat to there rule, people are calling for the fallen to lead them and they are now marching on the council chambers demanding there resignation, if he stays I fear they will try and kill him” he said and Marcus turned hearing the words.

He did not seem surprised or angry, the Mage simple nodded, a deep sadness that caught Corliss off guard shown in his eyes. “I am going anyway General; this isn’t done and I will finish it” he stated and turned back to the pile of clothing and weapons on the dresser in front of him. The Warden looked to the General and then to Marcus “What do you mean leaving, whats not done?” she asked where the hell did, he think he was going she wondered stepping into the room. Marcus finished putting on the shit and then the long leather coat, ensuring it was closed to the neck. He then slowly strapped the small stave on his waist and then picking up the curved, rune encrusted blade he placed that on his back, the hilt hanging over his shoulder in easy reach. “Warden, the Empress still has the capital, until she is taken down this will continue, she believes she is doing it for the good of the land, that is her justification and she will not stop until someone stops her” he said then turned to Dara and Maelen. “I am going to the capital, I am going to face the Empress, I have to, but you two don’t need to go, I would suggest you get as far away from me as possible” he said and Maelen shook his head “Not on your life, I am going to” he said and Corliss spotted the stupporn set of the young woman’s jaw and knew that Dara would go to.

She stood there a moment, and then came to a decision, one that surprised her and before she could change her mind or think it through “I am going too, you are going to need all the help you can get” she said wincing as she finished the statement. What the hell was she doing, she had no allegiance to this man and by all accounts he was more then capable of taking care of himself. But then Corliss knew, this was her land, she was a warden, she had taken an oath to protect those who live here and removing the Empress from power was part of that job.

Durass nodded “Follow me, we can’t go out the front” he began when the door burst open and Master Mage Patrice rushed into the house “Maelen” she called and the old man bolted to the top of the stairs “My love” he breathed and rushed down the stairs, gathering up the mage in his arms as they whispered too each other, tears rolling freely down there cheecks. Eventually they separated Marcus descended the stairs to the foyer and standing in front of the two he gently laid hands on there shoulders, whispering something the others couldn’t hear. Durass broke the moment “Follow me” he said urgently and motioning he descended the steps and began to go futher into the house.

Marcus was the last to follow and as he turned Corliss heard the front door explode as wood and metal shot into the house like so much shrapnel. She locked eyes with the young mage and watched as his eyes lit with power, blue light emanated from from as the wood and metal hit the unseen force of the shield he had conjured and fell harmlessly to the floor “They are here” hissed Durass as four large men entered the front of the house, pistols drawn they rushed in firing the slender weapons as blue energy erupted from the barrel exploding against Marcus’s shield as he nodded to the others to go “I will handle this” he said and turned to face the would be assasins.

The men continued to fire into the shield until she heard the audible click as the hammers dropped, the guns spent of ammunition. With a wave of his hand the four men were lifted off their feet slamming into the closest wall, as they slumped to the floor Marcus turned and followed the group.

“Whats going on General, why are people trying to kill the man that saved the city?” she asked looking back to see the man had not gotten up. Had he killed them she wondered Corliss had never seen that kind of power wielded, even by the mages she had known, he had merely slapped them away like annoying gnats. Durass never turned instead heading into the study and opening an entrance that Marcus was familiar with, the entrance to the catacombs opened before them and the General ushered the group down the spiral staircase. “The council is scared, people are calling for them to step down Warden, they see Marcus as a direct threat their rule, so they want to eliminate that threat” he said, and the Warden couldn’t believe what she was hearing.

“They would kill him, after what he did?” she asked shocked Durass followed down the spiral stairs close behind the Warden with Marcus trailing in case the would be assasins tried their luck. “They are scared Warden, the people see Marcus as the manifestation of the Legend, to them he is the fallen, the one who has come to lead our people, to save our people and they rail against those who stand against Marcus taking his place as the sole leader of the people. They see Marcus as a potential dictator and an outsider, that kind of threat must be dealt with in their eyes” he answered. “Sometimes fear makes people do stupid things Warden as is the case here” Durass finished as the group continued to descend.

Corliss looked at the solidly carved stairs as they descended down what looked like the middle of a tree. Once they reached the bottom, the low light highlighting the change from the solidly carved wood to ancient stone.

An old man stood silhouetted in the hall, as soon as Marcus laid eyes on him, he smiled, walking over and embracing the elder man. “Do not blame them Marcus, they are scared, and they do not think clearly” he whispered but loud enough for Corliss to hear him. “I know, I go to face the Empress elder, I go to end this” he said lowering his head the elder chuckling “I know, its inevitable my child, The Empress will try to turn you, the fact that you are still alive tells me she thinks she can, be wary Marcus, there has not been a power like you on this planet in centuries, many will try to lure you or worse to get that power” he finished.

Marcus bowed respectfully to the old man, he gently laid his hand upon the young man’s head and whispered words in a language that Corliss did not understand. When he had finished, the old man turned and shuffled deeper into the caverns of this stone complex. Durass called to the group and motioned for them to follow as he took them down winding passages moving faster as he tried to get Marcus and the other mages to safety.

The narrow stone hall opened up and light spilled in from an opening at the end, as they emerged from the stone hall Corliss found herself standing I the woods a large wooden door standing open as four guards stood sentry around it once they were all out Durass motioned to the guards and they closed the large wooden cover, locking it and covering it with moss and branches making it virtually impossible to spot unless you knew where to look.

At the bottom of the hill stood four horses all saddled and packed with supplies, Durass works fast she mused, moving towards the animals and spotting her own horse now freshly supplied. “Marcus” Durass called as the young mage stepped down the hill towards the horses. Both he and Corliss turned to see the man smiling as he reguarded the young man “I have one more gift for you” he said and with a motion of his hand a rider emerged on one of the large white cats, the animal was breathtaking, its muscles flowed easily under its fur pelt as it moved towards them.

The amber eyes of the beasy moved in the way only a predator’s eyes could as it reached Durass, the rider climbed down Marcus ignoring everyone stepped over to the large cat and began to stroke its head whispering to the animal as he did. The beast began to slowly utter a long languid pur as he did. Bieng this close to the creature was both exciting and scary she reflected looking it over with astonishment. Where had they come from, she wondered, knowing the first ones had changed the Silvans, had they also changed the animals she wondered, or were these something native to the northern dominance. Marcus turned to the General “Thank you General, I am honored by your gift” he said and walked up next to the creature, pulling himself up and into the saddle. Moving downt he hill on the creature Corliss watched as the horses stepped around nervously, the cat eyeing them the way, well the way a cat would a mouse Corliss thought walking down after the animal.

Ten minutes later the group rode for the border, Marcus and his cat in the lead, mostly because when the beast was behind the horses, they were a bit skittish they had come to find out. Corliss smiled at that and shook her head patting the rifle saddled within easy reach as she quietly thanked the Silvan’s for there hospitality as the group left the protection of the forest and into the lowlands of Vicor. The group rode hard south, heading for the capital of Vicor, Corliss spent the next two days in conflict within her mind. This man, this young mage had incredible power had saved the Silvan people and now meant to dethrone a sitting Empress, but could he be trusted she wondered. What could a person with that kind of power do, how could they stop someone like that.

The other Mages did not seemed bothered by his abilities nor did they seem to doubt the young man, all four of them following him without reservation, would it come down to her if this man needed to be stopped, of needing to be put down should he try and take power for himself, should he try and continue the Empress’s work. She thought about this for a full day and finally resolved

herself, she knew she would die, that someone would kill her if she were to try but if this Mage were anything other then someone who could put right that which the Empress had done, if he tried to become the new ruler of this land then Corliss would put him down once and for all. The third day they set out as the sun began to rise and everything was as quiet as the previous two until around midday when the young mage stopped, in the middle of a field turning the large cat in circles as he seemed to sense something.

“Whats he is doing?” Corliss whispered to Dara who had come to ride next to her, the two had become friends since rescuing Maelen and Dara enjoyed her company. It was obvious she had feelings for Marcus, but he didn’t even seem to really notice the young lady, Corliss could see the hurt in her eyes when no one was looking but she could hide it well. “I don’t know, it looks like he senses something, or might see something, wait” she said and everyone did, sitting silent as Marcus continued to circle, until finally pointing the large white cat west he bolted towards the horizon, everyone racing to catch up.

Corliss pushed her horse fast as she caught up to the large cat. “Where are we going Marcus?” she asked annoyed and for a moment she didn’t think he was going to answer and then he pointed into the distance. “There is a Seer, one of the Empress’s chosen in this direction” he simply said and then urging the big cat pulled away from the horse riding fast and with a purpose towards the

Empress’s chosen.

They rode long enough that Corliss began to doubt the young mage until they crested a ridge as the silhouette of a village wall came into view. “Maybe he was right” Corliss whispered reaching into the pack and pulling out the farseer, putting it to her eye she looked through the glass bringing the large village into view. She quickly made out the ten guards surrounding the collection of people and then, there on the stage was a man in a black robe standing on a dais and judging by the motions of his hands, he was lecturing those gathered.

The people surrounding the dauis were not there voluntarily as she could make out the faces, the fear as they looked at the soldiers patrolling around the group. Putting the device back into the back, Corliss pulled the rifle checking to ensure it was loaded and then checked both pistols, she knew they were, but the action was almost ingrained into her. “Whats the plan?” she asked as Maelen also leaned in Marcus quiet as they continued to move forward towards the village, finally he spoke his voice almost distracted as he seemed to be concentrating on something. “Take the guards, the Seer is mine” he said.

As they approached Corliss pulled the slender pistols and thumbed back the hammers, holding them down by the horse’s side keeping them out of view. The two guards at the gate perked up as the group approached and Corliss smiled as they noticed the large cat approaching with a rider on it. Corliss began to raise the pistols but before they were even level with the two guards they were flung backwards slamming against the wall on either side of the large entrance, Corliss looked over to see Maelen lowering his hands the old man smiling and nodding at the Warden. She nodded her thank you, better to be silent as long as they could be, she thought. But that ended quickly as Marcus slipped off the large cat, whispering to the animal he strolled towards the open gate and walked in. Corliss scrambled to join him, coming down off her horse she holstered the pistols and grabbed the rifle, rushing to catch up with the young mage.

They were close enough Corliss could hear the robed Seer talking at the group and she knew the moment he noticed the new arrivals, Maelen and Dara bringing up her flank as Patrice stayed with the horses. His voice died in his throat as the Seer turned to reguard Marcus and the Warden. “Guards, take them” the Seer announced camly and no sooner had he said it then Corliss’s rifle began to sing as blue lines of energy spat out of the barrel dropping first one, then four and finally eight of the soldiers before anyone could respond.

Marcus pulled his short mages stave and quickened his step as he approached the Seer. “You will not see the end of the day Chosen, you will surrender or die” he announced. The Seer’s face broke into a smile and with a quick gesture of his hand power flew at the two of them. The Young Mage struck out with the stave, knocking away the spell as a portion of the outerwall exploded into a maelstrom of splinters.

The smile died on the Seer’s face “I am the chosen of the Empress, you will die for your insolence mage” he announced Corliss turned to the rest of the guards as they rushed at the two of them. Ten more shots as guards dropped one after another, a few of them shot the single shot rifles but Dara took care of that, putting up a shield that caught the rounds protecting Corliss as she sheathed the rifle across her back and pulled the pistols. Spinning them as they did one full circle her thumb caught the hammer pulling them both back.

She aimed firing, spinning the pistols again and catching the hammer with her thumb. The ten guards she had seen were down, but as they continued to approach more spilled from the stone keep, Corliss spinning the pistols and pulling the hammer, shot after shot and the guards went down as they left the building. Then came the audible click as she fired the pistols dry. Holstering them she caught sight of Marcus as he continued to approach the seer at almost a leisurly pace, the Seer threw fire and lightning every spell knocked away casually as he continued to approach the robed mage.

Corliss grabbed the mahogany hilt, pulling the old sword from her back, Soldiers having given up on the pistols, every shot blocked by the mages protecting her also pulled their blades. Reaching behind her, she plucked one of the hatchets and holding out the weapons she beckoned the guards, inviting them to die.

The soldiers came at her, rushing as screams of rage escaped their lips and swords swung towards her. She parried and blocked, spinning and striking for all she was worth, soldier after soldier went down one finally landing a cut along her arm. Corliss screamed spinning the hatchet and driving the pick into the soldier’s head. He dropped like a sack of potatoes as the one behind him arced down with his own sword. Corliss brought up hers to block, but the wound on her arm made her weak and the Soldier easily knocked the blade out of her hand. She saw the malicious grin spread across his face as the sword arced back upward, aiming for her head. Jumping back, she felt the air as the blade barely missed her cheek. Driving out with the hatchet she caught the man in the side of the neck as blood erupted from the artery covering her arm in the warm red liquid.

She saw the next soldier, his sword swinging down as she tried to pull the hatchet from the first soldiers’ neck, but it wasn’t fast enough, and she watched as the weapon began its arc downward. Then suddenly he wasn’t there anymore as if a giant hand had come and slapped him across the yard the man hit the side of the stone keep, the sound of his bones shattering echoing across the common’s and she looked to see Dara standing there, breathing hard from the exerction, Nodding a thank you Corliss finally pulled the hatchet and picked up her sword. Turning she surveyed the field, no more soldiers stood.

The warden turned in time to see the two Mages locked in battle, the long-handled daggers that the staves separated into flashing as the two parried, countered and struck. She knew as soon as she saw the two, how the fight would end. Marcus, his face was almost serene as he flashed out, blocking and parrying each blow. But the Seer’s face was a mask of concentration and fear as he desperately tried to land a blow.

Finally, he shoved the end of one of the staves at the ground and shot backward arcing back towards the dauis, at the apex of the leap he pushed out with the hilts of the daggers Marcus knocking the fire spell away almost casually. Before he could land the Young Mage pointed his own daggers at the Seer, the black robed figure stopping abruptly in the air and hanging there. Marcus smiled before driving the Seer into the ground, picking him up and repeating it four more times. It was obvious that by third time the Lord Seer was very much dead.

Standing over the body Marcus’s face was devoid of emotion as Maelen and Dara began to care for the workers who had been injured, gathering the groups they explained where to go as they treated them. Marcus however never moved, just stood over the body, staring down at the man for what seemed like forever before he finally turned and strolled towards the gate and his cat. He sat there on the large cat as Patrice came in helping to treat the commoners. Two hours later the group finally moved back to the horses, Marcus having sat out there, pointed towards the Capital and not moving, merely sitting there and waiting. “Hey, you okay?” Corliss called and the mage turned to reguard her “I am, just., Im fine” he finished seeming to want to say more then deciding against it. She eyed the man for a moment before mounting the horse. “Whats the plan Mage” she asked, and Marcus turned his cat slightly before urging the creature on. “I am going to kill the Empress, just make sure no one bothers us” he said moving out.

The mage looked preoccupied, almost as if he were having a conversation with himself as he rode, but Corliss let him be. She would keep watch on him, if he somehow tried to join the Empress or take her place, she would have to take care of him, Corliss reloaded her pistols and rifle as she rode contuinging to eye the Mage. The group rode for two more days before the capital came into view.

They rode towards the Capital, towards the Empress and towards the battle that would decide the face of Vicor and its people.
